html:
The First Sudanese Civil War was fought from 1955 to 1972 between the government of Sudan and southern rebels seeking autonomy or independence for the south.

Under the Anglo-Egyptian condominium the British had governed the mainly Christian and traditional south apart from the Arab and Muslim north. When Sudan moved to independence, which came on 1 January 1956, northerners took most posts. Southern soldiers mutinied at Torit in August 1955, and from the 1960s the Anyanya rebels fought a guerrilla war.

Hundreds of thousands died. The Addis Ababa Agreement of 1972, signed under Nimeiry with help from Haile Selassie, gave the south its own government. It held for a decade, until the second war began in South Sudan.
sum: The First Sudanese Civil War was fought from 1955 to 1972 between the government of Sudan and southern rebels seeking autonomy or independence for the south.
